# UI/UX Skill: Professional Design & Brand Compliance

This file is a concise guide for implementing Sopra Steria UI. It contains the minimum actionable rules, a short "Quick Start", and links to deeper reference material.

## Quick Start
- **Purpose:** Build accessible, brand-compliant UI with pragmatic patterns.
- **Component classes:** Use the `ssg-` prefix for all custom components (example: `ssg-btn`).
- **Brand tokens:** Use the provided CSS variables (see "Brand Tokens").
- **Accessibility:** Ensure text meets 4.5:1 contrast, logical tab order, and visible focus states.
- **Project types:** Applies to plain HTML/CSS and component-based frameworks (Blazor, React, Vue, Angular, etc.). Use each framework's preferred file conventions (for example: `.html`/`.css`, `.razor`/`.razor.css`, `.jsx`/`.css`, `.vue`).
- **Components:** Refer to the minimal component index at the end; full examples live in `references/`.

## Core Philosophy
Keep interfaces simple, fast to scan, and accessible. Match UI complexity to user needs and prioritise clarity and predictable keyboard workflows.

---

## Architectural Context (Clean Architecture)

This skill covers **Presentation Layer** implementation in clean architecture:

- **DO** use this skill for UI components, pages, navigation, display logic, and user interaction
- **DON'T** implement business logic, data validation rules, or database access in the Presentation Layer
- **DO** inject business logic via application services (dependency injection)
- **DO** keep components thin — they should format data for display and delegate orchestration to services

**Key principle**: The Presentation Layer is the outermost layer; dependencies point inward toward Domain (never outward).

See [clean-architecture skill](../skills/clean-architecture/SKILL.md) for the full architecture model.

---

## When to Use
- New components or pages in any web framework (Blazor, React, Vue, Angular) or plain HTML/CSS
- Accessibility or brand compliance updates
- Component implementations following Sopra Steria patterns

## Scope
Plain HTML/CSS and component-based web projects. Focus areas: accessibility, brand tokens, component patterns, responsive layouts, and framework-agnostic implementation guidance.

## Workflow & Capabilities

### Project Type Detection
Detect project type from repository context and adapt guidance accordingly:
- **Framework projects**: Look for framework files (e.g. `.razor`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.html`), package manifests, or build configs.
- **Plain HTML/CSS**: Look for standalone `.html` and global stylesheet files.
- **Ask if unclear**: If ambiguous, ask which framework or file conventions the user prefers.

### Implementation Notes
- Use semantic HTML and accessible ARIA patterns.
- Prefer small, focused components with `ssg-` class names and clear public APIs.
- Structure styles with CSS variables and component-scoped styles (CSS modules, scoped styles, or framework equivalents).
- Follow framework conventions for component files and styling; keep presentation, markup, and behaviour appropriately separated.
- For plain HTML: include DOCTYPE, meta viewport, and a global stylesheet with the CSS variables below.

---

### Editing Existing UI
Audit markup and styles, apply `ssg-` patterns, verify contrast and keyboard navigation, run quick visual checks in target browsers.

---

## Browser Support & Testing
Target recent browsers (Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari). Test: visual rendering, contrast (4.5:1), keyboard navigation, and responsive breakpoints (mobile/tablet/desktop).

---

## Framework Guidance (brief)
- Follow your framework's component communication patterns (parameters/props, events/callbacks, and context/state APIs).
- Keep components small and testable; prefer explicit inputs over implicit global state.
- Lifecycle and re-rendering behavior should follow the framework's best practices; adapt examples in `references/` to your chosen framework.

## Brand Tokens (Sopra Steria)
Use the primary palette first. Do not change signature tokens.

Primary colors:
- Dark purple: `#4D1D82` rgb(77, 29, 130)
- Light purple: `#8b1d82` rgb(139, 29, 130)
- Red: `#cf022b` rgb(207, 2, 43)
- Orange: `#ef7d00` rgb(239, 125, 0)

Secondary colors: 
- Dark: `#1d1d1b` rgb(29, 29, 27)
- Very dark purple: `#2A1449` rgb(42, 20, 73)
- Grey: `#a8a8a7` rgb(168, 168, 167)
- Light grey: `#ededed` rgb(237, 237, 237)
- White: `#ffffff` rgb(255, 255, 255)

CSS variables (place in a global stylesheet):

```css
:root {
  --color-dark-purple: #4D1D82;
  --color-light-purple: #8b1d82;
  --color-red: #cf022b;
  --color-orange: #ef7d00;
  --color-black: #1d1d1b;
  --color-very-dark-purple: #2A1449;
  --color-grey: #a8a8a7;
  --color-light-grey: #ededed;
  --color-white: #ffffff;
  --brand-gradient: linear-gradient(45deg, var(--color-dark-purple) 0%, var(--color-light-purple) 15%, var(--color-red) 60%, var(--color-orange) 100%);
}
```

## WCAG 2.1 Essentials (condensed)
- Contrast: text must meet 4.5:1 against its immediate background.
- Keyboard: logical tab order and visible focus states.
- Motion: respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Forms/tables: proper `<label>`/`scope` usage.
- Glass/gradients: decorative halos okay; overlays with text must use alpha ≥ 0.8 or otherwise guarantee 4.5:1 contrast.

---

## Design & Layout (brief)
- Prioritise clarity: white space, clear grouping, and predictable focus.
- Rounded corners: 12px for cards, 8px for buttons.
- Max content width: 1200px.

(Glassmorphism guidance preserved in references for engineers.)

### Color Usage
- Primary actions: Dark purple `#4D1D82`.
- Maintain 4.5:1 contrast for text against its overlay.
- Focus: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(77,29,130,0.4)`.

### Typography
- Line height: 1.5 body, 1.2 headings. Weights: 400/500/600.

### CSS Class Naming
Use `ssg-` prefix for custom components (e.g., `ssg-btn`, `ssg-card`). Keep Bootstrap utility classes where they help (grid, spacing, flexbox).

## Accessibility Best Practices (RGAA 4.1.2 / WCAG 2.1)

**Form Fields & Labels**
- Every input must have a `<label for="id">` linked to the input's `id`
- For errors, add `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-describedby="error-id"` to link error text
- Group related fields with `<fieldset>` + `<legend>`; use `<fieldset role="group">` with `aria-labelledby` if needed

**Interactive Components**
- All buttons, tabs, accordions must have visible `:focus-visible` outline (≥ 2px, brand color)
- Tabs: use `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`
- Modals/Dialogs: trap focus, close on Esc key, return focus to trigger on close
- Accordions: use `aria-expanded`, `role="region"`, `aria-labelledby` for each panel

**Tables & Data**
- Add `<caption>` for table context
- Use `scope="col"` for header cells; add `id` to headers
- Data cells use `headers="header-id"` to associate with headers
- Complex tables: add `role="table"`, `role="rowgroup"` for screen readers

**Colors & Contrast**
- Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (normal) / ≥ 3:1 (large text, UI components)
- Never rely on color alone; add text, border, or icon to convey status (alert type, button state, etc.)
- Icon-only components: add `aria-label` for screen readers; decorative icons use `aria-hidden="true"`

**Keyboard Navigation**
- Tab order must be logical; avoid skipping focusable elements
- Arrow keys for tabs (Left/Right), modals (Esc to close), dropdowns (Up/Down)
- All interactive elements reachable via keyboard; no traps

**Semantic HTML & Document Structure**
- Use `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<section>`, `<main>`, `<footer>` for landmarks
- Heading hierarchy: avoid skipping levels (e.g., `<h1>` → `<h2>` → `<h3>`, not `<h1>` → `<h3>`)
- Use semantic elements instead of generic `<div>`: `<button>` instead of `<div class="btn">`, etc.
- Page must have descriptive `<title>` and declared `lang` attribute on `<html>`

**Live Regions & Announcements**
- Status messages: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`
- Alerts: `role="alert"`, `aria-live="assertive"`
- Form errors: link to field with `aria-describedby`

**Images & Icons (Thème 1)**
- Informative images: `<img alt="descriptive text">` or `<svg role="img" aria-label="...">`
- Decorative images: `<img alt="">` or `<i aria-hidden="true">` for icons
- Icon-only buttons: always add `aria-label` to convey button purpose
- Complex images/charts: provide `<figcaption>` or linked description

**Links & Navigation (Thème 6)**
- Link text must be meaningful and unambiguous (avoid "click here", "more", "link")
- Example: ❌ "Click here for more" → ✅ "Read full accessibility guidelines"
- External links: indicate with icon + text or `aria-label="opens in new window"`
- Dropdown/menu links: ensure keyboard navigation with Arrow keys

**Motion & Animations (Thème 13)**
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS media query; disable animations for users who set it
- Auto-playing animations/videos: ≤ 3 seconds or user-controllable
- Avoid rapid flashing (> 3 flashes/sec); avoid content that flashes at 3–39 Hz
- Example: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation: none !important; } }`
